steps: Uncrate
Remove the crate top, supports and plastic cover, then the lag bolts holding the stove body to the pallet (7/16" wrench).
Fit legs (leg model)
Loosen the four bolts holding the Leg Adapter, slip the legs between the flange and washers, seat the cast guides in the Ash Box flange notches and tighten. The pedestal or leg kit must be attached.
Ash cleanout (optional)
Remove the front cover and left-side knock-out, discard the cleanout hole cover plate, gasket the ash dump tube and bolt it up from below; fit the ash pan.

Remove the front cover

  • Pedestal model: remove the center screw of the Ash Drawer Front Cover Plate and lift it to free the bottom tab.
  • Leg model: remove the two screws (one on either side) holding the Leg Ash Box front cover.

Then remove the knock-out on the left side at the top of the opening.

Install the ash dump (p. 13)

  1. Remove the Ash Cleanout hole cover plate and gasket from under the stove; discard the plate.
  2. Fit the supplied gasket around the upper tube of the Ash Dump mechanism.
  3. Insert it from underneath up into the hole and over the two bolts, release handle facing forward on the left side, in the slot in the Pedestal or Leg adapter.
  4. Refit the nuts on the carriage bolts and tighten to gently compress the gasket.

Finish by installing the new Ash Pan in the Pedestal or the Leg Ash Box.
Floor protection
Non-combustible ember protection: USA 16" front and 8" to the sides of the fuel loading door opening, plus under the connector and 2" beyond each side; Canada 18" firing side, 8" other sides.
Set clearances
Place the stove to the rating-label clearances for the connector type. Shielding can reduce them with approval under CSA B365 or NFPA 211; use a listed double-wall connector for close clearances.
Chimney & connector

ULC-S629 / UL-103HT listed stainless or lined masonry chimney, 6" flue, 15 feet minimum system height, own flue. Single-wall: 6" 24 gauge black, crimped ends down, 3 sheet metal screws per joint; or a listed double-wall connector.
Install chimney & pipe
Plumb-bob the flue center to ceiling and roof, clear joists and rafters, install the listed chimney through to the rain cap, then fit the connector's crimped end inside the collar with three screws.

1. Choose the position from the clearances diagram; position the stove and floor protection.
  2. Mark the ceiling and roof hole with a string and plumb-bob hanging over the exact center of the flue pipe.
  3. Check the location won't interfere with floor joists, ceiling joists or rafters; adjust and reconfirm clearances.
  4. Install the listed chimney from the ceiling through to the rain cap per its maker's directions (may include framing in holes).
  5. Slip the crimped edge of the smoke pipe inside the stove collar and secure it with three screws through the holes in the collar.
  6. Add the remaining lengths up to the finished chimney height using the manufacturer's approved adapter; a slip section makes this easier.

Figures 11 and 12 (pp. 18–19) show a listed insulated chimney and a masonry chimney with a 6" S.S. liner. Offsets: screw every joint of connector, offset elbows and chimney with at least three sheet metal screws and use the chimney maker's listed offset support.
Combustion air
Room air enters through the Ash Box Enclosure, or bring outside air through the floor or wall with 4" metal flex and the 4" Intake Starter. Secure the stove to the structure when using outside air.
Through-wall pass-through
If the connector passes through a combustible wall, use an NFPA 211 system: A 12 in., B 9 in., C 6 in. or D 2 in. minimum to combustibles. Maintain the vapour barrier.

Per NFPA 211-2013 (pp. 20–21). The vapour barrier must be maintained wherever the chimney or other components penetrate to the exterior.

System A · 12 in. (305mm)Minimum 3.5 in. (90 mm) brick wall with 12 in. (305 mm) of brick from the fireclay liner (5/8 in. (16 mm) wall) to combustibles
System B · 9 in. (229mm)Solid-insulated listed chimney length, same inside diameter as the connector, 1 in. (25.4 mm) or more insulation, 9 in. air space
System C · 6 in. (152mm)24 gauge connector in a ventilated 24 gauge thimble with two 1 in. (25.4 mm) air channels, 6 in. of glass fiber insulation
System D · 2 in. (51mm)Solid-insulated listed chimney section 2 in. larger than the connector, 12 in. (305 mm) minimum length, 1 in. spacing, 2 in. air space

Figure 11 (p. 18) marks a 12" [300mm] minimum first section of pipe for the alternate up-and-out layout and notes the unit may be harder to start; give the first section as much vertical length as possible.

Confirm connector wall pass-throughs: the rating label (p. 3) says not to pass a chimney connector through a combustible wall or ceiling; p. 16 allows passage through a combustible wall or partition when the installation conforms to CAN/CSA-B365, and pp. 20–21 show these through-wall systems.
Mobile home
Listed double-wall connector and ULC-S629 / UL-103HT chimney, outside air, no horizontal connector; lag to the floor with two 1/4-20 x 2" or longer screws. Never in a sleeping room.

• Do not install in a sleeping room. Maintain the structural integrity of the floor, wall and ceiling/roof.
  • Attach the stove to the floor with two 1/4-20 x 2" or longer lag screws, using the leg anchors (hooked around the levelling bolt in each leg) on the leg model, or through the holes in the sides of the pedestal base.
  • Outside air supply must be used.
  • Use a listed double-wall connector and a compatible ULC-S629 or UL-103HT listed chimney. The rating label adds: horizontal connector not permitted in mobile homes.
  • Do not connect to a chimney flue serving another appliance.

Mobile-home clearances are on the rating label (p. 3) and drawn in Figure 17; see the Clearances card.

light.title: Lighting a fire
light.html:
Never use gasoline, lantern fuel, kerosene, charcoal lighter fluid or any similar liquid to start a fire or to "freshen up" one.

  1. Slide the air control to High, all the way to the left, and open the door.
  2. Put crumpled newspaper in the center of the stove. Criss-cross several pieces of dry kindling over it, then add a few small pieces of dry wood on top.
  3. Light the paper. Leave the door open about 1/2" (13mm) to 1" (25mm) until the kindling is fully in flames.
  4. Add a few small logs and close the door.
  5. Once there's a good bed of coals and the wood has charred, set the air control where you want it.
Build the fire right on the firebricks. Don't use a grate or andirons to raise the wood.

Your first few fires

The paint bakes on during the first 2-3 fires and gives off smoke and fumes that can bother some people. Open all the windows and doors while it cures, and follow the Stove Bright (Forrest Paint) sheet that came with the stove. Smoke detectors may go off more often for a while. Don't disconnect them.

air.title: Using the air control
air.html:
The air control sets how hard the fire burns. High ("H") is all the way to the left; "L" is low.

  • Starting and reloading: use High. Don't use it for anything else. It's only for starting or preheating fresh loads.
  • Settling in: once the wood has charred, turn it down to the setting you want. Every home is different, so find yours by trial and error and note it for next time.
  • Smoke pouring down the glass (a "waterfall") means you turned it down too soon or too far.

For the cleanest burn, leave the air fairly wide open for the first 10 to 30 minutes after loading. After about 30 minutes you can turn it down a lot without much smoke.

The stove has a factory-set minimum burn rate. Altering it is against federal regulations, and tampering with the air control voids the warranty and can be very hazardous.

With the optional blower

At "L", run the blower on Low; between "L" and "H", pick any speed. Set the rocker switch on the fan housing to Auto so the fan starts as the stove heats up and stops after it cools, or to Man to control it yourself.

reload.title: Reloading & overnight burns
reload.html:
Adding wood

  1. Move the air control to High and give the fire time to brighten.
  2. Open the door slowly so smoke doesn't puff back into the room.
  3. Load the logs endwise with space for air to flow between them. Mix shapes and sizes, and use only dry wood.
  4. Don't stack wood so high that opening the door would be hazardous.

Small loads burn cleanest: two or three logs at a time, or 1/4 to 1/2 of a full load.

Overnight burns

Unsplit logs work best. Char the load completely on the highest setting before you turn the air down for the night. Never try an overnight burn with green or wet wood.

Restarting in the morning

  1. Open the door, rake the hot embers toward the front, add a couple of dry split logs and close the door.
  2. Set the air control to High. The logs should catch within a few minutes.
  3. Once the wood has charred, reset the air control.
Confirm the longest log: the manual says logs up to 18" (457mm) on p. 7 but lists a maximum wood length of 20 inches on p. 3 (16-18 inches is called ideal).

wood.title: Choosing and testing wood
wood.html:
Burn natural wood only. Air-dried, seasoned hardwood generally burns cleaner and more efficiently than softwood or green wood. Season it for six months or more and store it under cover, away from open flame and heat.

Test a piece

Put a large piece on a good, large bed of coals:

  • Dry: it's burning on more than one side within one minute.
  • Damp: it turns black and lights within three minutes.
  • Soaked: it sizzles, hisses and blackens without lighting in five minutes. Don't burn it.

Wet wood smolders, makes heavy smoke and creosote (tar that builds up in the chimney), gives little heat and tends to go out. It can cut heat output by up to 25%.

Never burn

Garbage, salt-water wood, treated wood, coal or charcoal, solvents, yard waste, railroad ties, manure or animal remains, anything with rubber, plastic or asbestos, construction or demolition debris, petroleum products, paints or thinners, and paper, cardboard, plywood or particleboard. Salt-water wood and garbage contain chlorides that eat metal and void the warranty. Never barbecue in the stove.

Fire starters made from paper, cardboard, sawdust or wax are fine for lighting.

glass.title: Cleaning the glass
glass.html:
Clean the glass only when the stove is cold, using fireplace glass cleaner. Never use abrasive cleaners, and never scrape it with anything that could scratch it.

What the deposit tells you

  • Light brown and dusty, wipes off easily: good burning and dry wood. Your pipes and chimney are probably fairly clean.
  • Black and greasy, hard to remove: wet or green wood and too slow a burn. The same heavy deposit is building up in the chimney at least as fast.

If the glass keeps getting dirty, the door gasket may be leaking. Check the gasket and the door latch.

Protect the glass

  • Don't slam the door, and make sure no logs stick out to hit the glass when you close it.
  • Cracked or broken glass must be replaced before you use the stove again. Use only 17-1/2" (445mm) x 9-1/2" (241mm) x 5 mm ceramic glass from your dealer.
If the plated door needs cleaning, use mild soap and water only. Abrasive cleaners void the warranty.

ash.title: Removing ashes
ash.html:
Remove ashes only when the stove is cold. Once the ash is 3" (76mm) to 4" (102mm) deep and the fire has burned down and cooled, take out the extra, but leave about 1" (25 mm) on the firebox floor to help keep a hot charcoal bed.

Using the optional ash dump

  1. The handle is under the ash lip on the left. Pull it out 1/2" (13mm) and turn it clockwise to unlock the ash dump.
  2. Hold the handle open and pull ashes into the opening. Leave large embers in the stove; they still hold heat.
  3. Release the handle and push it in to lock. Make sure the ash dump door is properly closed, then fill the cavity with the remaining ash, level with the firebox floor.
  4. Lift out the ash pan, empty it into a metal container and put it back so it's seated properly.
Never burn with the ash dump door open. It creates a hazardous condition.

Getting rid of ashes

Use a metal container with a tight-fitting lid. Set it on a non-combustible floor or on the ground, well away from anything that can burn, and keep it closed until every cinder is thoroughly cool. Don't put other waste in it.

chimney.title: Creosote & chimney fires
chimney.html:
Slow, smoky fires leave creosote (a tar-like residue) inside the chimney. If it ignites, it burns extremely hot. Some creosote is unavoidable; regular inspection and cleaning is the answer.

  • Have the chimney and connector pipe inspected at least once every two months during the heating season, and remove creosote once it's 3 mm or more.
  • Until you know your stove, check for creosote daily. Weekly cleaning may be needed in mild weather; monthly is usually enough in the coldest months.
  • Burn dry wood, don't turn the air down too soon after loading, and avoid very hot fires from trash, cardboard or Christmas tree limbs.

Signs of a chimney fire

Flames and sparks shooting out of the top of the chimney, a roaring sound, or the chimney vibrating.

If it happens

  1. Close down the air inlet on the stove.
  2. Call the fire department.
  3. Get ready to leave. Everyone should know the plan and where to meet outside.
  4. Afterwards, have the chimney cleaned and checked for stress and cracks before your next fire, and check the combustibles around it and the roof.
Keep a fire extinguisher handy, and make sure everyone at home knows the plan.

care.title: Routine checks
care.html:
Look for cracks, heavy corrosion, burned-out sections and bad warping. Call your dealer if you find damage. Running the stove with broken parts can damage other parts and may void the warranty.

WeeklyFirebrick (cracks) · door gasket (sagging, placement, damage)
MonthlyBrick rails and their tabs · air riser tube at the back of the firebox · back of the airwash chamber · baffle locking pin · boost tube cover
When the chimney is cleanedBaffle and top baffle board · baffle gasket · top heat shield and its bolt · brick rails · manifold
BlowerVacuum the grill openings at least every six months

Door gasket

The 7/8" (22mm) fiberglass rope gasket needs only light pressure to seal. Inspect it now and then, and replace it if needed using the DR46.GLKIT kit from your dealer.

Baffle

Some warping is normal, up to 1/4" (.65cm). Replace the baffle if it's warped more than that, cracked or broken. Never run the stove with the baffle or its insulation removed.

Keep the front of the firebox, where boost air comes in, clear of ash buildup.

safety.title: Safety & over-firing
safety.html:
• The stove is hot while it's running. Keep children, clothing and furniture away. Hot glass causes burns: don't touch it until it's cooled, and never let children touch it.
  • Keep the loading door closed while burning and open it only to add wood. The stove isn't designed for open-door burning.
  • Never use gasoline, lantern fuel, kerosene, lighter fluid or similar liquids, and keep them well away from the stove while it's in use.
  • Keep stored wood, furniture, newspapers and anything else that burns out of the clearance area and the space you need for loading and ash removal.
  • Smoke and carbon monoxide detectors are strongly recommended where the stove is installed.

Signs of over-firing

A glowing red top or vent pipe means the stove is over-firing. An uncontrollable burn or any glowing red stove part or chimney means too much draft. Over-firing can permanently damage the stove and chimney, can be hazardous if it isn't corrected, and may void the warranty.

Smoke leaking into the room at the stove or pipe joints means too little draft. One cause is a plugged or restricted chimney; have it inspected and cleaned.

warranty.title: Warranty at a glance
warranty.html:
Pacific Energy's warranty covers the original registered purchaser.

Limited lifetime (10 years)Parts only: porcelain finish, glass (thermal breakage only, not impact), plating, firebox and baffle
3 year comprehensiveParts and labor on any defective part, including blowers, speed controls and thermal switches

Not covered

  • Labor under the lifetime coverage; firebox rails and heat shields are left out of it.
  • Firebrick, gaskets and ceramic fiber blankets.
  • Parts showing misuse, abuse, improper installation, accident, lack of maintenance or modification.

Excessive draft, heating too large an area, or contaminated fuel (high sodium, plastics, chemicals) can wear the stove early and may void the warranty.

Making a claim

Contact your Pacific Energy dealer with proof of purchase, the purchase date, the model name and the serial number. Register online at pacificenergy.net/register. The serial number is on the certification label and the manual cover.

This is a summary. The full terms are in the official PDF.

Emissions certified to the EPA 2020 crib wood standard using Method 28R. The rating table and label cover both the Summit LE and Summit Classic LE.

specOutside.title: Combustion air
specOutside.html:
Air comes from the room (through the opening in the Ash Box Enclosure) or from outside. Outside air is necessary for mobile homes and optional for residential installs; consult the local code or CAN/CSA-B365. The rating label also lists the outside air kit as required for alcove installation.

Through the floor

  • Air must come from a ventilated crawl space or be ducted to the outdoors.
  • Leg model: hole for 4" metal flex behind the ash box enclosure; attach the 4" Intake Starter to the Ash Box Enclosure and connect to the floor with 4"(100mm) i.d. metal flex pipe.
  • Pedestal model: 4" (100mm) hole anywhere inside the pedestal perimeter, covered with a 4" x 4" (100 mm x 100 mm) rodent screen; leave the cover on the back of the pedestal in place.

From behind the stove

  • 4"(100mm) air intake through the wall; 4" Intake Starter over the rear hole of the Ash Box enclosure, metal flex to the intake.
  • Pedestal model: move the rear cover plate to the hole under the pedestal, then fit the Intake Starter at the rear.

Figures 11–12 show a 4" (102 mm) diameter air inlet with rodent screen, hooded or a 90° elbow turned down; with a well-ventilated crawl space it need not be extended outside.

Using outside air in a residence requires securing the stove to the structure so the duct can't be dislodged.

Keep the room well ventilated: negative pressure can pull fumes into the living area, and in extreme cold an exposed chimney can ice up and let flue gases in.

specBlower.title: Optional blower
specBlower.html:
Kit#WODC.BLOWB · three prong power cord

Can be installed at any time; follow the kit's instructions. Route the power cord away from the heater, never beneath it. Auto uses a sensing device to start and stop the fan with stove temperature; Man bypasses it. Vacuum the grill openings at the back and bottom of the casing at least every six months. Blowers, speed controls and thermal switches fall under the 3 year comprehensive warranty.

Confirm the blower current: the manual gives 115 volts A.C.-1.02 amps on p. 23 and 115V, 60HZ, 1.0 AMP on the rating label (p. 3).

Blower electrical rating: '115 volts A.C.-1.02 amps' (p. 23) vs rating label 'FAN ELECTRICAL RATING: 115V, 60HZ, 1.0 AMP' (p. 3).

Rating label says 'DO NOT PASS A CHIMNEY CONNECTOR THROUGH A COMBUSTIBLE WALL OR CEILING' (p. 3); p. 16 allows passage through a combustible wall or partition per CAN/CSA-B365 and pp. 20-21 give NFPA 211 through-wall systems A-D. Also flagged in step8.

U.S. floor protector sides: p. 14 text gives 8" (203 mm) to the sides of the fuel loading door opening; rating label gives U.S.A. G 16 in., H 5 in., I 0 in. (p. 3). Label letters are defined only in its drawing, so the two may be measured from different points.
Rating label alcove and mobile-home sidewall-to-connector (D) values read '26 in. / 690 mm' and '28 in. / 693 mm'; the inch and mm figures do not correspond.
Baffle gasket part number: 'replace with gasket #139.5' (p. 10) vs 'Gasket, Baffle ... 80000365' in both parts lists (pp. 26-27).

review.notes: Models: the manual covers Summit LE and Summit Classic LE with one rating label (also listing the Alderlea T6 LE; only its SUMMIT values were used), one efficiency/emissions table and one set of clearances. It distinguishes them only by the p. 11 dimension drawings (Summit pedestal, Summit leg, Summit Classic) and separate parts lists (p. 26 Summit LE; p. 27 Summit Classic LE, which lists leg parts only plus color side shields, top, ash lip and trivet). Dimensions were not transcribed: the p. 11 callouts carry no width/depth/height labels in the text, and some Summit Classic inch/mm pairs don't line up. Clearances come from the rating label's named A-F rows; the A-F grouping (SUMMIT vs ALDERLEA T6, single/double wall, alcove, mobile) was checked against the raw reading-order extract of p. 3, as was the efficiency table pairing (LHV 80%, HHV 74%, ideal 16-18 in, max 20 in). The unlabeled callouts in the p. 15 and p. 22 clearance drawings and the '54" [1.37m] Minimum' callout in Figure 11 were not transcribed. Label single-wall E/F values (14.5 / 16.9 in.) sit below the label's own 18 in. single-wall connector minimum; the label's asterisk explains them ('as tested, pipe shield may be required'), shown as a warning, not a conflict. Alcove width ('LARGEUR 4 PIEDS/1.2M') appears only in the French label text; not used. No French-only gas/safety block and no scrambled text. Minor, not flagged in drawers: p. 2 says EPA limits for heaters sold after May 15, 2015, p. 3 says May 15, 2020; metric roundings vary (18" = 457/455/460 mm, 16" = 406/405 mm, 8" = 203/205/200 mm); installer certifications named differently on pp. 5, 15, 22. Stale cross-references in the manual: p. 17 'see Figure #3, Page 7', p. 22 'see .pg.16' (outside air is p. 17) and 'see page 17' (chimney is p. 16), p. 25 'see page 11'. Parts lists print 'Bony Black' for the Classic side shield (top and ash lip say 'Ebony Black') and 'Bruched Nickel' for a leg finish; shown as printed or omitted. Catalog fields the manual doesn't state: heating area, cordwood max BTU, burn time, firebox volume, glass area, non-catalytic, Extended Burn Technology, plate-steel top. Catalog btu_output_epa 41,275 and log_length_max_in 20 match p. 3 but not p. 2 / p. 7 (see conflicts).
